summary: Nalini Devdas works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr, also studying under teachers including Paul David Devanandan and Steven Collins, and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

Nam-lin Hur works in Japanology, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Princeton University under Helen Hardacre. He was a Harvard postdoctoral fellow and became a professor at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and served as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including Derge Gonchen Monastery. He taught at Southwest Minzu University (~1958–1960) and was Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

Nancy Grace Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Columbia University and earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas, Michael Hahn, and Somadeva Vasudeva.

Nancy Hock works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams and held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held an academic post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011) and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and Superintendent of the Archæological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies (~1980–1985) and held teaching posts (~1985–1993) at Tohoku University, followed by a professorship at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).
Naoki Nabeshima is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Toshifumi Goto and earned her PhD from Tohoku University in 2002. She later served there as a specialized researcher (attested 2012).

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at Cardiff University and a Chancellor's Fellowship at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Professor and Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1927–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (~1974–1979).
Naoya Funahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at Otani University (attested 1981) and worked as an encouragement researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Narada Mahathera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Ceylon University College and trained under traditional teacher Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1917–1955).

Narayan Hemandas Samtani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a Research Fellow and earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961), subsequently serving as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).

Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He spent his career holding academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1967–1975, ~1985–1999, attested 1990).

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1976). He held posts at Kobe University (~1983–1997) and the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies (1989), later serving as Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1997–2010).
